name: Leg curl
angleNote: Knee flexion: 0° = leg straight (start), 120° = heel towards the buttocks. Hip at the origin.

segments.massNote: Segment mass as a fraction of body mass, and centre of mass as a fraction of the segment length from its proximal end, from de Leva's adjusted Zatsiorsky-Seluyanov table (young adult males). The lower leg includes the foot (combined centre of mass along knee → ankle; the foot's own position is approximated).
segments.massSource: de Leva P (1996). Adjustments to Zatsiorsky-Seluyanov's segment inertia parameters. J Biomech 29(9):1223–1230. doi:10.1016/0021-9290(95)00178-6 (Table 4, males)
segments.note: Hip→knee and knee→ankle in metres, typical adult.

strengthCurve.label: Knee flexor strength
strengthCurve.note: Relative isometric knee-flexion torque vs knee flexion, peak about 30°, measured seated with the hip flexed about 70° (tested 0–103°). Relative curve = cos(C2·(θ − C3)) with the 18–25-year-old male means of Table 3; points only inside the tested range, so the app holds the end values flat beyond it. Peak torque default from the same table's C1 (young men, scaled to 73 kg and 1.75 m). The seated test position matches the seated leg curl best; lying, the hamstrings are shorter and somewhat weaker (not modelled). Variants correct this for the hip angle (two-joint hamstrings): see each variant's strength note.
strengthCurve.source: Anderson DE, Madigan ML, Nussbaum MA (2007). Maximum voluntary joint torque as a function of joint angle and angular velocity: model development and application to the lower limb. J Biomech 40(14):3105–3113. doi:10.1016/j.jbiomech.2007.03.022

muscles.name: Hamstrings
muscles.note: Cross the hip as well; their length (and strength) depends on hip angle, which these weights ignore.

muscles.name: Gastrocnemius
muscles.note: Calf muscle that also crosses the knee and helps flex it.

phases.name: Mid-range
phases.text: Lying or standing with an ankle weight, the lower leg passes horizontal near 90°, where gravity's torque peaks.

phases.name: Fully bent
phases.text: Heel near the buttocks; hamstrings are weakest here.

variants.name: Lying leg curl machine

camProfile.note: Effective radius in metres: joint torque per unit of stack weight, including any lever or pulley ratio. Illustrative shape, not measured from a specific machine.

variants.notes: Face down with the hip straight. The pad is behind the ankle; lifting the lower leg's weight also adds torque until it passes vertical (90°).

strengthScale.note: hip straight, so the hamstrings are shorter: knee-flexion strength about 61% of the seated test's. Guex et al. measured 62 Nm with the hip straight vs 110 Nm at 90° of hip flexion (knee at 45°); the base curve was measured with the hip at about 70° (101 Nm by interpolation). Measured at one knee angle only, so the factor is applied across the range.
strengthScale.source: Guex K, Gojanovic B, Millet GP (2012). Influence of hip-flexion angle on hamstrings isokinetic activity in sprinters. J Athl Train 47(4):390–395. doi:10.4085/1062-6050-47.4.04 (Table: isometric, knee at 45°, 10 sprinters)

variants.notes: Hip bent 90°, so the hamstrings work from a longer length. Here the lower leg's weight helps the curl. The extra strength from the longer hamstrings is not modelled.

strengthScale.note: hip bent 90°, hamstrings lengthened: about 109% of the base curve's strength (Guex et al.: 110 Nm at 90° of hip flexion vs about 101 Nm at the base curve's 70°). Measured at one knee angle only.
strengthScale.source: Guex K, Gojanovic B, Millet GP (2012). Influence of hip-flexion angle on hamstrings isokinetic activity in sprinters. J Athl Train 47(4):390–395. doi:10.4085/1062-6050-47.4.04 (Table: isometric, knee at 45°, 10 sprinters)

variants.name: Standing leg curl (ankle weight)
variants.notes: Torque = (m·L + lower-leg weight)·g·sin(knee angle): nothing at the start, largest with the lower leg horizontal at 90°.

strengthScale.note: hip straight, so the hamstrings are shorter: knee-flexion strength about 61% of the seated test's. Guex et al. measured 62 Nm with the hip straight vs 110 Nm at 90° of hip flexion (knee at 45°); the base curve was measured with the hip at about 70° (101 Nm by interpolation). Measured at one knee angle only, so the factor is applied across the range.
strengthScale.source: Guex K, Gojanovic B, Millet GP (2012). Influence of hip-flexion angle on hamstrings isokinetic activity in sprinters. J Athl Train 47(4):390–395. doi:10.4085/1062-6050-47.4.04 (Table: isometric, knee at 45°, 10 sprinters)
